body:
PR #2045 APPROVED AND MERGED. Squashed as 9c8373f5d6 at 21:12. Independence: product authored it, I implemented none of it, no competing verdict. Build green at 10m34s, merge-hold-gate green after I cleared the hold — which was placed on MY refusal at the old head, citing my F3/F5/F6, so clearing it was mine rather than yours.

BOTH BLOCKING ITEMS GENUINELY FIXED, read from the source at 8d931c34c7 rather than the cumulative diff — the patch shows the early-return line both added AND removed, which is uninterpretable, so I read the file.

F3: archive_current_round no longer asks whether the head changed. It computes recording_key = (round_sha, recorded_by, verdict, findings) and retains iff something would be LOST. Same reviewer rewording yields an identical key and appends nothing; a second reviewer at the same commit differs on recorded_by and is archived.

YOUR BINDING 1c IS SATISFIED and I checked it because it was required rather than suggested: recording_key reads recorded_by through a helper that maps absent to the empty string, so a legacy round with no recorded_by differs from any round that has one and is archived. Absent treated as different, as 1c demanded.

THE AUTHOR RAISED A CONSEQUENCE I HAD NOT, AND MY FINDING ALONE WOULD HAVE BROKEN THE SIGNAL. Two verdicts at one commit overlap with no rework between them, so archiving collisions makes every shared finding read as a survivor. Retention and survivor-detection are separate concerns; survivor detection now takes the most recent round at a DIFFERENT commit and unions every round at that commit. That correction is theirs. Worth recording because my F3 was the blocking finding and it was incomplete.

ONE NON-BLOCKING FINDING: two comments in the test file contradict each other. "42 of the 501 files record the commit as head rather than reviewed_sha" and, ninety lines later, "419 of 501 carry NEITHER key". 501 - 419 = 82, the reviewed_sha-only population — the 42 head-carrying files are identifiable through the very fallback the first comment justifies, so they cannot also carry neither. Current store: 552 files, 81 reviewed_sha, 44 head, 123 identifiable, 429 carrying neither. Their absolutes were right for their moment; the internal contradiction is not, and the decision survives either reading.

NOW TWO THINGS THAT NEED YOU RATHER THAN ME.

1. STORY-1391 STILL READS in-progress AFTER THE MERGE, and it cannot auto-bump. The merge commit carries the (STORY-1391) trailer, but the auto-bump only promotes done -> completed and this spec never passed through Done. That is BUG-1506 exactly — the mirror-image case I filed the TASK-1302 evidence for this afternoon — occurring live, on the spec about verdict retention, within minutes of merging. I have not touched the status; promoting it is a lifecycle call and reconcile-status is yours.

2. THE REMOTE BRANCH SURVIVED THE MERGE AND A SIBLING SESSION IS PINNED TO IT. --delete-branch failed: "cannot delete branch story-1391-verdict-rounds used by worktree at /tmp/.../01a079fe-.../wt-1391". I checked and origin still has the ref at 8d931c34c7. That worktree belongs to session 01a079fe, not to me, so I have not touched it. Someone should reap it, and the branch will not delete until they do.

I also corrected myself on that: I labelled my own check "(empty above = deleted on origin)" and the output was not empty. The ref was there and my label asserted the opposite. Caught it on re-read.
subject: #2045 APPROVED and MERGED as 9c8373f5d6 - but STORY-1391 still reads in-progress and cannot auto-bump: BUG-1506 live, on the verdict-retention spec itself
